accessibility: The dialog is named "New comment" and described by its description; Where is a radio group with its legend, each card a radio with its hint as description; an error is an alert; Comment says it needs text through its disabled state and the empty box.
constraints: Built only from Adapter Widgets (Stack, Text, Button, Icon, TextInput, Alert, Panel dialog, RadioGroup, Radio); no Widget outside the Adapter catalog.

The two Where states, the typed text and each error are shown by Variants; the dialog is a Panel with a shadow over the page, not a dimmed Workbench behind a Modal. The one-line Workspace place is a sample string per Locale because the app composes it from two strings.
The strings of the app are copied under the same Locale keys; the View name binds through value; the Commenting as line (a field help takes no value) and the message are sample strings per Locale.
Every visible string is bound with $i18n except identities (names); en-US and zh-TW keep identical key sets.
Visual language follows the Quiet Canvas design system in DESIGN.md.
entryConditions: A reviewer holding the key to write Review threads chose New comment in the Reviews inbox, or Comment on Workspace in the command palette; the dialog opens over the page with focus in the message box.

The base state is opened from a page that has no View: the only place is the Workspace, said in one line, and the message is empty, so Comment is disabled. Opened from a View's Reviews, the Where choice offers the Workspace or that View.

The render context selects one Workspace viewport preset, one Locale and one theme; the dialog is Workbench chrome, so its text follows the Workbench language and is baked here per Locale. The member, the View name and the message are sample content.
spec.intent: Show the New comment dialog of the Workbench as built from Adapter Widgets only: how a reviewer starts a thread without a canvas, from the Reviews inbox or the command palette, about the product as a whole or about the View they came from, and what the dialog says when the post fails.
interactionRules: The dialog always states where the comment goes, as the Workspace (feedback about the product as a whole, which never sits on a View's canvas) or as the View as a whole, which is anchored to its RootShell; it never defaults to one silently. To comment on a Widget, comment mode on the canvas stays the way.

Comment, or ⌘↵, posts the thread and its first message; the dialog closes and opens the thread. A failed post keeps the text and says so; Retry sends again. When the thread was created and its message was not, the dialog says so and the button becomes Retry, which posts only the message.
Cancel and Esc close the dialog and keep nothing; the dialog says "Commenting as" the signed-in member.
